'''Gordon M. Keller''' is a Canadian scientist recognized for his  research on applying [[developmental biology]] findings to ''in vitro'' [[pluripotent stem cell]] differentiation. He is currently a Senior Scientist at the [[Ontario Cancer Institute]], a Professor at the [[University of Toronto]] and the director of the [[McEwen Centre for Regenerative Medicine]].<ref>University Health Network [http://www.uhnresearch.ca/researchers/profile.php?lookup=12091 "Research Profile: Gordon Keller, PhD"]</ref>

== Biography ==
Keller was born in 1952 in [[Melville, Saskatchewan|Melville]], [[Saskatchewan]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Behind the Breakthrough Podcast - University Health Network Season 4 - Dr. Gordon Keller |url=https://www.uhn.ca/corporate/News/UHN_Podcasts/Behind_the_Breakthrough/Documents/BTB-S4E2-Keller-Transcript.pdf |access-date=14 December 2023}}</ref> and was raised on a farm.<ref>The Globe and Mail [https://www.theglobeandmail.com/report-on-business/saskatchewan-native-dr-gordon-keller-a-leader-in-regenerative-medicine/article1216161/ "Saskatchewan native Dr. Gordon Keller, a leader in regenerative medicine"]</ref> He completed his Bachelor of Science at the [[University of Saskatchewan]].<ref>University of Saskatchewan [http://awards.usask.ca/faculty/recipients/keller.php "Honorary Doctor of Science - Gordon Keller"]</ref> He completed his PhD in [[Immunology]] at the [[University of Alberta]] in 1979, and completed his postdoctoral fellowship with the Ontario Cancer Institute in 1983. He then began his career in Switzerland and Austria. In 1990, he moved to the United States. Initially, Keller was at the National Jewish Centre for Immunology and Respiratory Medicine in Denver, CO and later moved to the [[Mount Sinai School of Medicine]] in New York City, NY. In 2007, Keller returned to Canada to assume his current role and established his laboratory at the [[MaRS Discovery District|MaRS Centre/Toronto Medical Discovery Tower]].<ref name="CCRM" /> In 2016, Keller co-founded Toronto-based BlueRock Therapeutics with [[Lorenz Studer]] for the development of iPSC-derived cells for clinical transplantation.

== Scientific research ==
[[File:FASEB Adler et al 2010.webm|thumb|Embryonic stem cell derived cardiomyocytes published by the Keller group in ''[[The FASEB Journal|FASEB]]'' 2010]]
In 1997, Keller's team was the first to successfully isolate the developmentally significant [[hemangioblast]]—a  multipotent precursor cell that can differentiate to the [[hematopoietic]] and [[endothelial cell]] fates—using [[embryonic stem cell]] technology.<ref name="Choi">{{cite journal |vauthors=Choi K, Kennedy M, Kazarov A, Papadimitriou JC, Keller G |title=A common precursor for hematopoietic and endothelial cells |journal=Development |volume=125 |issue=4 |pages=725–732 |year=1998|doi=10.1242/dev.125.4.725 |pmid=9435292 }}</ref>

The Keller group's research includes the differentiation of pluripotent stem cells to the [[endodermal]] lineage: [[hepatocytes]],<ref name="Hans">{{cite journal |vauthors=Han S, Dziedzic N, Gadue P, Keller GM, Gouon-Evans V |title=An endothelial cell niche induces hepatic specification through dual repression of Wnt and Notch signaling |journal=Stem Cells |volume=29 |issue=2 |pages=217–228 |year=2011 |doi=10.1002/stem.576 |pmid=21732480 |pmc=3437666}}</ref> [[cholangiocytes]] and [[pancreatic]] progenitors;<ref name="Nostro">{{cite journal |vauthors=Nostro MC, Sarangi F, Ogawa S, Holtzinger A, Corneo B, Li X, Micallef SJ, Park IH, Basford C, Wheeler MB, Daley GQ, Elefanty AG, Stanley EG, Keller G |title=Stage-specific signaling through TGFβ family members and WNT regulates patterning and pancreatic specification of human pluripotent stem cells|journal=Development |volume=138 |issue=5 |pages=861–871 |year=2011 |doi=10.1242/dev.055236|pmc=3035090 |pmid=21270052}}</ref> as well as to [[mesodermal]] cell fates: [[cardiomyocytes]],<ref name="Kattman">{{cite journal |vauthors=Kattman SJ, Huber TL, Keller GM |title=Multipotent flk-1+ cardiovascular progenitor cells give rise to the cardiomyocyte, endothelial, and vascular smooth muscle lineages|journal=Developmental Cell|volume=11 |issue=5 |pages=723–732 |year=2006 |doi=10.1016/j.devcel.2006.10.002 |pmid=17084363|doi-access=free }}</ref> [[chondrocytes]],<ref name="Craft">{{cite journal |vauthors=Craft AM, Ahmed N, Rockel JS, Baht GS, Alman BA, Kandel RA, Grigoriadis AE, Keller GM |title=Specification of chondrocytes and cartilage tissues from embryonic stem cells|journal=Development|volume=140 |issue=12 |pages=2597–2610|year=2013 |doi=10.1242/dev.087890|pmid=23715552|doi-access=free}}</ref> [[T lymphocytes]]<ref name="Kennedy">{{cite journal |vauthors=Kennedy M, Awong G, Sturgeon CM, Ditadi A, LaMotte-Mohs R, Zúñiga-Pflücker JC, Keller G |title=T lymphocyte potential marks the emergence of definitive hematopoietic progenitors in human pluripotent stem cell differentiation cultures|journal=Cell Reports|volume=2 |issue=6 |pages=1722–1735|year=2012 |doi=10.1016/j.celrep.2012.11.003 |pmid=23219550|doi-access=free }}</ref> and [[myeloid]] precursors.<ref name="Sturgeon">{{cite journal |vauthors=Sturgeon CM, Ditadi A, Awong G, Kennedy M, Keller G |title=Wnt signaling controls the specification of definitive and primitive hematopoiesis from human pluripotent stem cells|journal=Nature Biotechnology|volume=32 |issue=6 |pages=554–561|year=2014 |doi=10.1038/nbt.2915 |pmid=24837661 |pmc=4152856}}</ref>

== Honours ==
Keller holds a Tier I [[Canada Research Chair]] in Embryonic Stem Cell Biology (2013-2020).<ref name="CCRM" /> He serves on the Scientific Advisory Boards of the [http://www.ccrm.ca Centre for Commercialization of Regenerative Medicine] and Stemgent, and is also a founding member and past president (2005-2006) of the [[International Society for Stem Cell Research]].<ref name="CCRM">Centre for Commercialization of Regenerative Medicine [http://www.ccrm.ca/GordonKeller "Lead Scientist: Gordon Keller"]</ref> In addition, he is a senior editor for the journal ''Development''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://dev.biologists.org/site/misc/edboard.xhtml|title=''Development'': Editorial Board}}</ref> In 2025, Keller won the [[International Society for Stem Cell Research|ISSCR]] achievement award for his work in "laying the foundations for all modern [[directed differentiation]] approaches".<ref>{{Cite web |title=Gordon Keller Receives the 2025 ISSCR Achievement Award for his Seminal Work in Regenerative Medicine |url=https://www.isscr.org/isscr-news/gordon-keller-receives-the-2025-isscr-achievement-award-for-his-seminal-work-in-regenerative-medicine |access-date=2025-05-18 |website=International Society for Stem Cell Research |language=en-US}}</ref>
